Two streams. One patient state.

Separate EHR records and chronological wearable measurements join through patient ID. Every feature uses current or past data.

Age, prior diagnosis, HbA1c, BMI and a hypothetical genetic marker.

Predictions checked against later observations.
Actual later values from independently generated synthetic patient timelines provide the test labels.
Five forecasting methods, tested on the same patients
Lower forecast error is better. Higher alert precision and spike recall are better. All results are synthetic.
New spike = current glucose ≤180 mg/dL and actual glucose >180 mg/dL exactly 2 hours later. This does not detect every crossing within the interval.
Dedicated two-hour spike-risk classifiers
These classifiers drive the dashboard alerts; the five methods above benchmark glucose-value forecasting with a fixed 180 threshold.
Does combining both streams help?
Regression diagnostic: the same model family is retrained using each source separately. Event columns apply the point-forecast threshold, not the dashboard classifier.
What happens with imperfect sensors?
Regression stress test: keep future outcomes unchanged and perturb only past inputs. Event columns use the point forecast, not the dashboard classifier.
How the evaluation is protected
Method references: patient-group and chronological evaluation · probability calibration.
Every alert has an outcome
Model selection on validation patients
The winner is chosen before test scoring. Test metrics do not influence which model is deployed. Models are trained in Python; the browser runs the exported fitted parameters.
Synthetic meals, circadian rhythms, patient differences and correlated noise generate continuous glucose trajectories. Future meal variation is not supplied to the predictor.
Performance across patient groups
Regression subgroup diagnostics using the fixed point-forecast event threshold. Small, synthetic groups do not establish clinical fairness.
What this proves: a reproducible ML pipeline, two-stream fusion, a continuously updated virtual patient, two-hour event forecasts and comparison with future observations. What still needs research: real patient data, clinical validation and prospective evaluation. Hypothetical genetic features have no asserted real-world association.
